questions.question: Which new Zurich capability allows synthetic monitoring checks to run from existing MID Server infrastructure without additional deployment?

options.text: Run Monitors Directly from MID Servers

explanation.correct: Zurich adds the ability to run synthetic monitors directly from MID Servers. This means zero additional infrastructure—customers can leverage existing MID Servers for synthetic tests, reducing TCO and going from zero to monitoring in minutes. See: https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-blog/zurich-release-highlights-what-s-new-for-itom-synthetic/ba-p/3405038

wrongAnswers.explanation: MID Server Health Monitoring is not the Zurich synthetic monitoring feature.
MID Server Synthetic Agent is not the correct name for this feature.
Discovery-Based Monitoring is not the Zurich synthetic monitoring capability.

references: Zurich Release Highlights - ITOM Synthetic Monitoring

source.excerpt: You can now execute synthetic tests directly from your existing MID Server infrastructure!

questions.question: What new Zurich feature allows you to create HTTP endpoint CIs directly from the 'New Monitor' configuration screen?

explanation.correct: Zurich introduces Streamlined Endpoint CI Creation, allowing you to create new endpoint records right from the 'New Monitor' configuration. This is valuable for greenfield deployments or organizations still building their configuration management practices. See: https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-blog/zurich-release-highlights-what-s-new-for-itom-synthetic/ba-p/3405038

wrongAnswers.explanation: Quick CI Creator is not the correct name for this Zurich feature.
Inline Endpoint Builder is not the Zurich feature name.
Monitor-to-CI Wizard is not the correct name for this capability.

references: Zurich Release Highlights - ITOM Synthetic Monitoring

source.excerpt: You can now create new endpoint records right from the 'New Monitor' configuration.

questions.question: What new Zurich capability ensures synthetic-generated alerts are automatically routed to the correct team when an endpoint fails?

explanation.correct: Support Group Assignment in Zurich makes it easy to automatically assign synthetic-generated alerts to specific support groups. This ensures alerts route directly to the team that owns the endpoint, with clear ownership and accountability. See: https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-blog/zurich-release-highlights-what-s-new-for-itom-synthetic/ba-p/3405038

wrongAnswers.explanation: Alert Routing Rules is too generic and not the specific Zurich feature name.
Team-Based Alert Dispatch is not the correct name for this feature.
Incident Auto-Assignment is not the Zurich synthetic monitoring feature.

references: Zurich Release Highlights - ITOM Synthetic Monitoring

source.excerpt: Support Group Assignment ensures alerts route automatically to the right teams with clear ownership and accountability.

questions.question: From which three locations can synthetic monitoring checks now run in Zurich?

options.text: MID Servers, ACC fleets, and ServiceNow instance
Discovery probes, ACC clients, and cloud agents
Edge servers, data centers, and MID Servers
Pattern engines, ACC fleets, and orchestration servers

explanation.correct: With Zurich, synthetic monitoring checks can run from MID Servers, ACC fleets, and your ServiceNow instance. This provides multiple layers of monitoring from any part of your ServiceNow architecture. See: https://www.servicenow.com/community/itom-blog/zurich-release-highlights-what-s-new-for-itom-synthetic/ba-p/3405038

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is not the correct combination of synthetic monitoring execution locations.
Edge servers and data centers are not the correct locations listed for Zurich.
Pattern engines and orchestration servers are not synthetic monitoring execution locations.

references: Zurich Release Highlights - ITOM Synthetic Monitoring

source.excerpt: You can now run checks from any part of your ServiceNow architecture: MID Servers, ACC fleets, and your ServiceNow instance.
